rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.title: Gulf states arrested over 1,000 for Iran war social media posts: Amnesty
rfi.description: More than 1,000 people have been arrested across Gulf states for sharing information or opinions related to the Iran-US-Israeli war, in what Amnesty International has described as a “widespread crackdown” on freedom of expression.

rfi.title: 'Choose France' summit puts AI at heart of Macron’s €93 billion investment drive
rfi.description: Foreign companies have pledged a total of €93 billion in investment at France's annual Choose France summit, President Emmanuel Macron announced on Monday, with artificial intelligence and data infrastructure projects accounting for the bulk of commitments.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion
rfi.description: Ethiopia holds parliamentary and regional elections on Monday that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party to win by a large margin, despite significant unrest across much of the country.

rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Bafana Bafana return to the World Cup chasing a first knockout stage
rfi.description: South Africa enter the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's 11th-ranked side in the Fifa standings. In the first instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at a nation making its fourth appearance at the finals.

rfi.title: Last hurrah:  Algeria's Riyad Mahrez
rfi.description: Riyad Mahrez will play for Algeria for the second time at the World Cup at the age of 35. In the fourth instalment of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks at the career of a striker who has risen from modest clubs to international stardom.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Football heroes: PSG victory toasted by thousands of fans in Paris
rfi.description: The French capital held a hero's welcome for Paris Saint-Germain players who won their second consecutive Champions League title with celebrations under heavy security after a night of revelry marred by unrest. The team was received by President Emmanuel Macron ahead of a victory parade which drew thousands of supporters.

rfi.title: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon
rfi.description: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

rfi.title: Last hurrah: Brazil's Neymar
rfi.description: Neymar will play for Brazil at the World Cup for the fourth time at the age of 34. In the third of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks back at the career of a striker who holds his country's record for both scoring and assisting goals.

euronews.title: ‘Sit back and relax’: White House Iran post goes viral and gets torn apart online
euronews.description: Echoing an oft-misattributed literary quote, Donald Trump's advice to his critics has been reposted by the official White House account. The post has gone viral, with many pointing out that repeating a deal with Iran is close does not make things better.

euronews.description: EU leaders are set to discuss the possibility of engaging in direct talks when they meet on 18-19 June. But the latest draft of the summit's conclusions suggests a mandate for a special envoy is still far away.

euronews.title: Pashinyan moves to defuse Russia tensions while pledging Armenia's sovereignty ahead of crucial vote
euronews.description: With the latest polls showing him on course for a landslide victory on Sunday, PM Nikol Pashinyan told Armenians – and Russia – that he is seeking a balanced yet sovereign approach to his foreign policy, as Russia continued to exert pressure by imposing more sanctions ahead of the crucial vote.

euronews.title: Bear injures four in residential area of Japan as annual number of attacks rises

Après la publication d’une méta-analyse de l’organisation indépendante Cochrane, trois spécialistes plaident pour une surveillance active afin de limiter le recours à une biopsie ou à des traitements aux effets éventuels négatifs.

france24fr.title: 🇸🇳 Sénégal : un nouveau gouvernement boycotté par Sonko

france24fr.title: Israël : la guerre pour seul horizon ? Parlons-en avec Sylvaine Bulle, Tamar Sebok et Anne Corpet
france24fr.description: Israël continue de mener cette guerre au Liban contre le Hezbollah, depuis le 2 mars que le Parti de dieu a rouvert le front en soutien à Téhéran. france24fr.title: RD Congo, quinze civils et un militaire tués dans une attaque à Beni

Les ADF, groupe terroriste d'origine ougandaise affilié à l'État islamique, ont commis un massacre au sein de la communauté pygmée. Ce nouveau massacre inquiète car c'est la première fois depuis plus de trois ans que le groupe frappe à l'intérieur de la ville.

observador.description: O cessar-fogo de abril não tem impedido Israel de alargar a ofensiva no sul do Líbano, o que deixa o Irão mais longe de um acordo com os Estados Unidos. Há outro Estreito em risco de fechar.

observador.title: Inflação acelera para 3,2%  na Zona Euro em maio
observador.description: De acordo com os dados do serviço de estatística da União Europeia, prevê-se que, em maio, a energia registe a taxa de inflação homóloga mais elevada, seguida dos serviços, da alimentação e álcool.

observador.title: MP acusa 22 arguidos de crimes económicos na venda de roupa
observador.description: Ministério Público defende que "os arguidos operam ao nível de organização de cariz internacional" e pede na acusação penas acessórias de expulsão para os que têm "nacionalidade chinesa".

observador.title: Intel fecha acordo com Foxconn para criar sistemas de IA
observador.description: A colaboração, revelada esta terça-feira na Computex, visa explorar arquiteturas complementares para responder às exigências das cargas de trabalho de IA.

observador.title: Movimento denuncia ressurgimento de poluição no Tejo
observador.description: O proTEJO pede a responsabilização legal e administrativa dos agentes poluidores identificados, incluindo a suspensão das licenças de rejeição de efluentes em caso de incumprimento

observador.title: Israel. Aprovada 1.ª votação para dissolução do Parlamento
observador.description: Knesset aprovou a primeira de três votações para antecipar eleições. A crise na coligação, provocada pelos ultraortodoxos, precipitou a queda do governo de Netanyahu.

observador.title: Suspeito de matar idoso em silêncio no início do julgamento
observador.description: No local do crime foi encontrada uma garrafa de cerveja, que para além dos vestígios biológicos coincidentes com o ADN do arguido, tinha vestígios palmares e digitais do mesmo, referiu a testemunha.

observador.title: Pai e filho condenados em Leiria a prisão por burlas
observador.description: Arguidos, de 25 e 58 anos, foram condenados a dois anos e nove meses de prisão por seis crimes de burla. Detidos enviavam mensagens às vítimas a pedir dinheiro fazendo-se passar por familiares.

observador.title: Iker Lecuona substitui Alex Márquez na Hungria
observador.description: Alex Márquez sofreu um violento acidente, em 17 de maio, após embater na KTM de Pedro Acosta, sofrendo uma fratura da clavícula e de uma vértebra no pescoço. Lugar será ocupado por Iker Lecuona.

observador.title: Chega propõe reforma aos 40 anos de descontos ou 65 de idade
observador.description: Ventura diz que o partido quer "garantir que quem tenha 40 anos de descontos possa reformar-se". Chega vai propor também que as "reformas milionárias sejam limitadas a 4.500 euros mensais".

observador.title: Braga recebeu a Cimeira da Indústria da Observador
observador.description: Ao longo de um dia inteiro, passaram pelo Theatro Circo alguns dos nomes mais relevantes da economia nacional na cimeira organizada pelo Observador, com a colaboração da AEMinho.

observador.title: PTRR publicado em Diário da República
observador.description: Plano prevê uma execução entre 2026 e 2034 e contempla "medidas de curto prazo com reformas e investimentos estruturais destinados a produzir impactos consistentes ao longo do tempo".

observador.title: As notícias das 13h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Morreu Rick Adelman, um dos melhores treinadores da NBA
observador.description: Adelman era o 10.º treinador com mais vitórias na NBA. "Vai ser recordado não apenas como treinador e jogador, mas como mentor para muitos na comunidade do basquetebol", refere a NBCA.

observador.title: Suspeito de regularizar 4 mil imigrantes fica em preventiva
observador.description: O advogado acusado de ajudar ilegalmente quatro mil imigrantes foi colocado em prisão preventiva. Empresário, acusado do mesmos crime, está sujeito ao pagamento de uma caução de 60 mil euros.

spiegel.title: Pflegeversicherung: Pflegebedürftige erhalten zu selten Zahnarztvorsorge
spiegel.description: Menschen, die gepflegt werden, erhalten einer Auswertung zufolge zu selten die Vorsorge, die sie benötigen. Dabei können Ärzte diese sogar gesondert abrechnen. Patientenschützer nennen den Zustand »nicht hinnehmbar«.

spiegel.title: Junge Auswanderer über Deutschland: »Wir wünschen dem Land nichts Schlechtes, aber es muss sich viel ändern«
spiegel.description: Immer mehr Deutsche verlassen ihre Heimat – so wie Marie und Alex. Hier erklären sie, warum sie sich für einen Neuanfang in Schweden entschieden haben.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Péter Magyar will Wolodymyr Selenskyj treffen, wenn Bedingungen erfüllt sind
spiegel.description: Unter Premier Orbán war Ungarn der große Bremser und Verhinderer in der EU, wenn es um Hilfe für die von Russland überfallene Ukraine ging. Sein Nachfolger Péter Magyar setzt ein anderes Zeichen, stellt aber auch Bedingungen.

spiegel.title: Verden: Mann wegen tödlicher Misshandlung seiner Mutter zu Freiheitsstrafe verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein 66-Jähriger hat im niedersächsischen Oyten seine Mutter so schwer misshandelt und verletzt, dass sie starb. Die Taten wurden dokumentiert, weil die Enkelinnen der Frau ein Babyfon im Schlafzimmer installiert hatten.

spiegel.title: AfD: Geheimdienstpolitiker warnen vor Spionagegefahr bei Russlandreise
spiegel.description: AfD-Abgeordnete reisen nach Sankt Petersburg. Kritik kommt aus den Regierungsparteien und von den Grünen. Der Vorsitzende des Geheimdienst-Ausschusses warnt: »Man kommt nicht unbeobachtet zurück.«

spiegel.title: Großbritannien und die Peter-Mandelson-Affäre: Das System M.
spiegel.description: Er kungelte mit Jeffrey Epstein, hielt Kontakt nach China oder Russland – und mischte im Innersten der britischen Regierung mit. 1500 Seiten Akten offenbaren den Einfluss des Diplomaten Peter Mandelson. Miserabel der Eindruck, den man von Premier Starmer gewinnt.

spiegel.title: Berlin-Neu-Hohenschönhausen: Straßenbahn entgleist und aufgerissen
spiegel.description: Im Osten Berlins ist eine Straßenbahn entgleist. Drei Menschen wurden schwer verletzt.

spiegel.title: Tofu: Warum die Produktion bei der Nachfrage nicht mehr mitkommt
spiegel.description: Tofu boomt in Deutschland, immer mehr Menschen setzen auf den Eiweißlieferanten. Aber viele Regale in den Supermärkten bleiben leer. Was es mit dem Engpass auf sich hat und warum es vorerst nicht besser wird.

spiegel.title: Blake Lively und Justin Baldoni stehen wohl vor neuem Rechtsstreit
spiegel.description: In ihrem schlagzeilenträchtigen Streit haben sich Blake Lively und Justin Baldoni unlängst außergerichtlich geeinigt. Die Schauspielerin verlangt nun aber erneut Geld von ihrem ehemaligen Filmpartner.

spiegel.title: KI: Wie der Chatbot von Meta Angreifern fremde Accounts öffnete
spiegel.description: Metas KI-Chatbot hat sich als allzu hilfreich erwiesen: Fremde konnten ihn austricksen, um die Kontrolle über prominente Instagram-Accounts zu erlangen. Und dafür brauchte es kein komplexes IT-Wissen.

spiegel.title: Rudi Assauer: Tochter und frühere Privatsekretärin angeklagt – Vorwurf des bandenmäßigen Betrugs
spiegel.description: Rudi Assauers Tochter pflegte den früheren Schalke-Manager in seinen letzten Lebensjahren. Nun sollen die 60-Jährige und Assauers Ex-Privatsekretärin vor Gericht. Der Vorwurf: bandenmäßiger Betrug.

spiegel.title: El Niño erwartet: Was das Phänomen für die Welt bedeutet
spiegel.description: Das Phänomen El Niño könnte 2027 zum heißesten Jahr der Geschichte machen. Was das für das Wetter in Europa und die Preise im Supermarkt bedeutet – und worüber Experten noch rätseln.

spiegel.title: Italien: Mailand empört über restaurierten Stier ohne »Glückshoden«
spiegel.description: Weil abergläubische Touristen darauf Pirouetten drehen, musste ein Stiermosaik in Mailand repariert werden. Doch nach der Restaurierung sind die berühmten »Glückshoden« beinahe verschwunden.

spiegel.title: Kölner Dom: Besucher müssen künftig zwölf Euro Eintritt zahlen
spiegel.description: Die Ankündigung sorgte für Debatten: Wer den Kölner Dom besichtigen will, muss künftig zahlen. Anders sieht es bei Gottesdienstbesuchern aus.

spiegel.title: AfD: Wie schützt man die Demokratie vor ihren Feinden, bevor es zu spät ist?
spiegel.description: Die rechtsextreme AfD greift nach der Macht – und in den Landtagen versuchen die anderen Parteien, noch eilig Gerichte, Parlamente oder den Rundfunk abzusichern. Wo das gelingen kann und wo es weiteren Schaden anrichtet: der SPIEGEL-Report.

spiegel.title: Auerswalde bei Chemnitz: Elf Rehkitze bei Mäharbeiten getötet – Anwohner erstattet Anzeige
spiegel.description: Erntemaschinen werden Rehkitzen häufig zum Verhängnis. Nun sind in Mittelsachsen elf Jungtiere gestorben. Anwohner hatten schon lange gewarnt.

spiegel.title: Zoll-Streit mit den USA: Handelsausschuss des EU-Parlaments billigt Deal
spiegel.description: Die EU und die USA entschärfen ihren Handelskonflikt. Der zuständige Ausschuss des Europaparlaments macht den Weg für Nullzölle frei. Im Gegenzug senkt Präsident Trump Einfuhrabgaben auf bestimmte Metalle.

spiegel.title: Israel: Knesset billigt in erster Lesung Gesetz zur Selbstauflösung
spiegel.description: In der Koalition von Regierungschef Netanyahu gibt es Streit, die Ultraorthodoxen pochen deshalb auf einen früheren Wahltermin. Eine weitere Hürde auf dem Weg ist nun genommen.

elpais.title: Feijóo esquiva en Barcelona la propuesta de negociar en Waterloo y con Puigdemont la moción de censura
elpais.description: “Devolveré la decencia a mi país con ayuda o sin ella”, asegura el líder del PP en su intervención en el  Círculo de Economía

elpais.title: El PSOE eleva ahora de 15.000 a 45.000 euros el importe que pagó a Leire Díez por labores de comunicación
elpais.description: El partido detalla los pagos a la exmilitante por su trabajo en Cantabria hace casi una década en un escrito al juzgado de Madrid que investiga una causa distinta a la que llevó a la Audiencia Nacional a enviar a la UCO a Ferraz

elpais.title: La guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, en directo | Trump abronca a Netanyahu por sus ataques en Líbano: “Estás jodidamente loco”
elpais.description: El republicano reprocha duramente al primer ministro israelí su postura en una llamada desvelada por ‘Axios’ y ante el temor de que se rompa la negociación con Irán | El ejército israelí emite la primera orden de desalojo en el sur de Líbano desde el anuncio del presidente de EE UU

elpais.title: La defensa de David Sánchez, a una testigo clave de las acusaciones: “¿Por qué no interpuso denuncia en 2017?”
elpais.description: Cristina de Frutos, que aspiraba al puesto que finalmente logró el hermano del presidente, insiste en sus sospechas sobre la adjudicación sin aportar pruebas

elpais.title: La princesa Leonor, primera paracaidista de la Familia Real
elpais.description: Zarzuela difunde imágenes de la heredera preparándose para saltar en Alcantarilla (Murcia) como parte de su formación militar

elpais.title: Condenado a dos años y medio de cárcel el dueño de los perros sueltos que mataron a dentelladas a una joven en Zamora
elpais.description: La jueza asigna la pena solicitada por la Fiscalía por un caso de 2023, en el que una jauría atacó a una mujer que transitaba por el campo

elpais.title: Presunta imparcialidad
elpais.description: El doble rasero judicial y policial acaba erosionando la legitimidad de un poder fundamental del Estado

elpais.title: Las reinas no fuman
elpais.description: El mensaje general de doña Letizia casi parecía dirigido a alguien en particular

elpais.title: Putin anuncia una “nueva dimensión” en su guerra contra Ucrania y mata al menos a 18 personas en un intenso ataque
elpais.description: La ofensiva del Kremlin, una de las peores de los últimos meses, golpea Kiev, Dnipró y Járkov y causa un centenar de heridos

elpais.title: Las banderas ultras de Abelardo de la Espriella
elpais.description: El vencedor de la primera vuelta, que ha empleado un tono misógino y homofóbico, es admirador de Milei y Bukele, promete recortar un 40% de la burocracia del Estado y quiere volver a debatir derechos que ya han ganado las mujeres y la población LGBTI frente al aborto y la adopción de niños

elpais.title: El Gobierno inyecta 260 millones a la empresa estatal de vivienda para construir 1.629 casas asequibles
elpais.description: Casa 47 gestiona ya 68 proyectos por todo el país, con los que espera levantar más de 3.000 inmuebles, según los datos del Ministerio de Vivienda

elpais.title: Diez entidades envían una carta al Papa para denunciar la cárcel que visitará en España: “La que más denuncias ha recibido”
elpais.description: La Xarxa Dret i Presó critica que el sistema penitenciario catalán presenta “síntomas de clara regresión” ante el uso de contenciones y los problemas de salud mental y suicidios

elpais.title: Jonathan Andic da la batalla de la opinión pública con la vista puesta ya en el jurado popular
elpais.description: El primogénito de Isak Andic, investigado por el presunto homicidio de su padre, fía la misión de revertir el relato a un investigador privado de la defensa

elpais.title: La inminente llegada de ‘El Niño’ echará “más leña al fuego de un mundo que se calienta”
elpais.description: La Organización Meteorológica Mundial insta a estar preparados ante el riesgo de aumento de los fenómenos extremos alimentados por este evento natural

elpais.title: Familias que sufren con la Selectividad: “Me da igual la nota, lo único que quiero es que se acabe ya la PAU”
elpais.description: El estrés de los progenitores ante la prueba de acceso a la universidad crece en paralelo al aumento de las notas de corte

elpais.title: Los destinos turísticos españoles empiezan a bajar precios ante el freno de reservas para verano
elpais.description: Los viajeros extranjeros retrasan las contrataciones a la espera de ofertas de última hora o barajan quedarse en sus lugares de origen por los costes de volar y alojarse en otros países

elpais.title: Mapa de sitios oficiales para ver el eclipse total de Sol: EL PAÍS actualiza el único buscador de puntos de observación
elpais.description: España se enfrenta al reto de acoger a millones de visitantes el 12 de agosto. Ayuntamientos y autonomías ya han elegido 190 miradores para gestionar concentraciones multitudinarias para contemplar el histórico fenómeno

elpais.title: Una concentración por Juan Carlos, el trabajador del SEPE de Mérida expedientado por atender a ciudadanos que no conseguían cita previa
elpais.description: El empleado se enfrenta a una posible sanción por ayudar a usuarios fuera del sistema de reserva mientras denuncia el colapso de la atención y la falta de personal en la oficina extremeña

republika.title: Guerra in Iran, le news di oggi. Nave Msc colpita dai pasdaran in un porto iracheno
republika.description: Tajani: “La pace? Sono gli Usa che devono fermare Israele”. Raid di Israele in Libano: almeno otto morti, tre sono bambini. Bozza del summit Ue: “Lavorare sulle sanzioni ai ministri estremisti di Israele”

republika.title: 2 giugno, 80 anni della Repubblica. La parata ai Fori, Mattarella: Costituzione nostra casa comune
republika.description: Al via le celebrazioni con la cerimonia al Milite Ignoto con il capo dello Stato, Crosetto, Meloni. Poi la sfilata ai Fori imperiali fino all’evento speciale in piazza del Quirinale

republika.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, news. Media: “Salgono a 18 le vittime dei raid russi in Ucraina”
republika.description: Palazzi in fiamme a Kiev. Ft: “Usa stanno discutendo idea armi nucleari in altri Paesi Nato”

republika.title: "Ebola non entrerà negli Usa”. Piano americano per portare gli infetti in Kenya. Esplode la protesta
republika.description: La Corte Suprema del Paese africano si oppone all’accordo segreto con Washington. Scontri e roghi nella base militare di Laipikia. Qui gli Stati Uniti stanno già costruendo un ospedale per isolare gli eventuali cittadini contagiati

republika.title: Propaganda Isis, resta in carcere il ventunenne fermato in Brianza. La gip: “Pericoloso socialmente”
republika.description: Convalidato il fermo di Zakaria Ben Haddi. Le sue parole: “Sì, quegli account sono miei ma non volevo fare apologia”

republika.title: Parata 2 giugno, fermati sei ambientalisti: preparavano un blitz all’Altare della Patria
republika.description: Gli attivisti di Extinction Rebellion fermati dalla polizia vicino al cantiere della metro con uno striscione di grandi dimensioni e fumogeni. Denunciati per invasione di terreni ed edifici, tre anche per resistenza

republika.title: L'ultima sfilata, poi il meritato riposo: oggi va in pensione Briciola, la mascotte dei carabinieri
republika.description: La cagnolina partecipa alla parata del 2 giugno per l’ultima volta. Divenne famosa nel 2015, con la capriola davanti a Mattarella

republika.title: Trump dirotta in chiave Maga i festeggiamenti per i 250 anni degli Stati Uniti
republika.description: Dall’annuncio di un arco di trionfo ai lavori per la Casa Bianca e per il Mall fino alla preghiera pubblica per celebrare le radici cristiane della nazione, le celebrazioni del 4 luglio sono diventate divisive. Ci sono star che annunciano boicottaggi. Bruce Springsteen e Tom Morello prevedono un concerto di popolo in vista delle elezioni di midterm

republika.title: Migranti, accordo Ue sui rimpatri: ok ai return hub in Paesi terzi e al foglio di via europeo
republika.description: Tra dieci giorni entrerà in vigore il nuovo Patto asilo – diverso dal protocollo Italia-Albania – e il governo Meloni dovrà ricorrere a un nuovo decreto con le principali disposizioni contenute nel ddl immigrazione ancora fermo in Senato e l’adeguamento alle norme europee, più la reintroduzione del blocco navale

republika.title: Xenia Fedorova, il volto dei media Bolloré che fa infuriare Parigi: “Propagandista russa”
republika.description: L’ex direttrice di RtFrance è stata ingaggiata dalle tv della galassia del miliardario: “Segno di pluralismo”. Ma per per il ministro degli Esteri Barrot è un favore a Putin. Glucksmann: “Toglietele il microfono, è una agente”

republika.title: Spese per l'energia, la Ue concede all'Italia una mini-clausola da 6,5 miliardi, durerà 18 mesi
republika.description: La deroga verrà illustrata domani in occasione della presentazione delle raccomandazioni economiche di primavera

republika.title: “Non respiro”. Un 18enne bianco viene ucciso in Inghilterra e “White Lives Matter” diventa virale
republika.description: Il drammatico caso di Henry Nowak, accoltellato a morte da un 23enne sikh a Southampton. L’assassino millanta alla polizia di essere vittima di un’aggressione razzista e gli agenti arrestano il ragazzo in fin di vita, che spira ammanettato dicendo “I can’t breathe”, come George Floyd a Minneapolis nel 2020. Furia di Farage e della destra inglese: “Una vergogna, sono i bianchi ormai a essere discriminati: questo è razzismo al contrario”

republika.title: La strage dei braccianti pakistani, uccisi in auto e poi dati alle fiamme. Fermate due persone
republika.description: Il rogo in una stazione di servizio sulla statale 106 nei pressi di Amendolara, nel Cosentino. Determinanti i filmati delle telecamere di videosorveglianza: “Chiuse le portiere, arsi vivi in macchina”

republika.title: Italia, quarti di nobiltà al Roland Garros. Cobolli, Berrettini e la notte di Arnaldi
republika.description: Flavio supera Svajda e affronterà Auger-Aliassime. Derby tra i due Matteo: uno elimina Cerundolo, l'altro rimonta Tiafoe al 5°

republika.title: John Travolta: “La vita mi ha messo alla prova ma non mi arrendo”
republika.description: Il divo di Hollywood al suo esordio da regista con “Volo notturno per Los Angeles” ora su AppleTv, racconta il successo di “Pulp Fiction” e il ruolo fondamentale della sua famiglia. E confessa “’La strada’ di Fellini mi segnò, mi fece capire che non avrei mai spezzato il cuore a nessuno”

republika.title: Da suddite a cittadine, il 2 giugno delle donne
republika.description: Come si arrivò al voto alle donne di ottant’anni fa nel referendum che suggellò la nascita della Repubblica? Lo racconta oggi la storica al festival La grande invasione di Ivrea. Ecco un estratto del suo intervento

republika.title: Kiev brucia. I russi mobilitano una forza d’assalto colossale contro l’Ucraina
republika.description: Mosca aveva annunciato un’offensiva “senza precedenti” contro la capitale, ma l’attacco è stato esteso a tutto il Paese

republika.title: Il tennis che ci emoziona anche senza Jannik
republika.description: Arnaldi, Berrettini e Cobolli, mai nella storia del tennis tre italiani erano arrivati insieme ai quarti di finale di uno slam.

nyt.title: Iran War Live Updates: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Pulling Back From Threat to Beirut
nyt.description: Under pressure from President Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel held off from attacking Beirut. But he vowed to continue Israel’s campaign against Hezbollah, which could threaten peace talks with Iran.

nyt.title: Hospitals See Diseases Resurge as Vaccinations Decline
nyt.description: Doctors nationwide are encountering more children with whooping cough, bacterial infections and other serious illnesses, as well as more adults refusing tetanus shots.

nyt.title: Extreme Water Shortages in the West, and Hegseth’s Pentagon Purge
nyt.description: Plus, the rocky, unpredictable race for California governor.

nyt.title: How Hezbollah Drones Changed Israel’s Strategy in Lebanon
nyt.description: An Israeli campaign that started with high hopes has devolved into a kind of impasse, with Hezbollah looking more capable than it did when the war began.

nyt.title: Trump Finds High-Wire Iran Negotiations ‘Very Boring’
nyt.description: President Trump told CNBC that he “couldn’t care less” if the negotiations with Iran break down.

nyt.title: Security Council Members Call for Israel to Withdraw From Southern Lebanon
nyt.description: The U.N. panel met after Israel had threatened to attack southern Beirut. President Trump said later that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed not to attack each other.

nyt.title: Trump Backs Off Plan for $1.8 Billion Fund That Drew Political Backlash
nyt.description: The fund has drawn backlash from critics who said it was a scheme to reward President Trump’s political allies with public benefits.

nyt.title: California Primary Elections: What to Watch in the Governor’s Race, L.A. Mayoral Race and More
nyt.description: The race to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom has been unpredictable for months, while Mayor Karen Bass of Los Angeles is trying to fend off two challengers.

nyt.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Iowa, Montana and Beyond
nyt.description: Democrats have a competitive Senate primary race in Iowa, where the party is hoping to make gains, while a smokejumper is running in a contested House primary in Montana.

nyt.title: Group Pledges $2 Million to Fight AIPAC in House Races
nyt.description: A super PAC created to counter spending from powerful pro-Israel groups will try to help Democrats critical of Israel’s wars and military actions.

nyt.title: Obama Center’s Two Sides: A Lovely Park and a Forbidding Tower
nyt.description: In Chicago, the $850 million Obama Presidential Center aims to remake a neighborhood with a 19.3-acre community hub and a brooding 225-foot museum.

nyt.title: Russia Launches Deadly Strikes on Kyiv After Threatening Ukraine for a Week
nyt.description: Moscow’s repeated warnings of a major strike, combined with the delay before it happened, seemed intended to inflict a psychological toll on the Ukrainian capital.

nyt.title: Russia Is Showing Signs of Weakness in Ukraine. So It Hits Harder.
nyt.description: The war has not been going the Kremlin’s way recently, with battleground losses and mounting casualties. With renewed strikes, Moscow hopes to gain a better position for negotiations.

nyt.title: As A.I. Makes Strides in Mathematics, Mathematicians Urge Caution
nyt.description: A week after OpenAI made headlines with an A.I.-generated proof, a new “declaration” by 16 experts raises concerns that the technology threatens math as a discipline.

nyt.title: What Ireland and Germany Can Teach Us About Birthright Citizenship
nyt.description: President Trump has argued that the United States is “stupid” for granting citizenship at birth. Most countries don’t do so, but that can create problems.

nyt.title: U.S. Was Asked to Blacklist Colombian Cartel Gold. It Was Also Buying It.
nyt.description: The request for sanctions, from Colombia’s defense minister, shows failures at both ends of the supply chain for illegal gold.

nyt.title: Mamdani Is Under Pressure to Act Amid Slowing Job Growth in New York
nyt.description: As New York City faces slowing job growth and broader economic concerns, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has not offered a detailed plan to create jobs.

nyt.title: Mamdani Advances 34th St. Bus Lane Plan That U.S. Had Blocked
nyt.description: The city is moving forward with a redesign of 34th Street in Manhattan that the White House halted last year after threatening to withhold federal funding for other transit priorities.

npr.title: EU strikes migration deal for more deportations and detention centers abroad
npr.description: The European Union has moved forward with an overhaul of its migration policy, aiming to ramp up deportations and build detention centers abroad. Critics compared the regulation to the immigration strategy of the Trump administration.

npr.title: Global conflicts push Sri Lanka's economy to the brink
npr.description: Sri Lanka was careening from crisis to crisis, then came the Mideast war. People say they've got no buffer left.

They definitely feature those, as does all good observational astronomy. The problem with statistics is, in order to get a clear definitive answer, you need lots of samples. phys-org.title: New mantises planking their way to urban dominance
phys-org.description: A team of scientists have discovered and named three new "leaf-planking" praying mantis species and recorded another mantis species turning up far from its assumed habitat. JCU Ph.D. candidate Matthew Connors recently discovered and named three new Snake Mantis species from the Kongobatha genus (K.serpens, K.spinosistyla and K.rufilinea), publishing his detailed observations of each species in the journal Zootaxa.

phys-org.title: Health-related ballot measures more likely to pass
phys-org.description: As voters are increasingly asked to decide complex health policy questions at the ballot box, new research from the Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis finds that health care-related ballot measures draw more voters to the polls and are more likely to pass than other initiatives—but they're also especially sensitive to opposition spending by special-interest groups.

phys-org.title: New tech enables scientists to see emperor penguins in darkness
phys-org.description: Research led by Professor Michelle LaRue from the School of Earth and Environment at Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) published in Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation shows that high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery can track emperor penguins through the Antarctic winter, opening a new way to monitor an endangered species during a critical stage of breeding.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Most biology education guidelines lack any connection to society, researchers explain why that's a problem
phys-org.description: Is it a doctor's job to get the best outcomes for their patients or to tell the truth? What happens when these two things are not aligned? These are questions that University of Washington students have to wrangle with in Biol 180: Introductory Biology. The goal, says Elli Theobald, UW assistant professor of biology, is to have students experience a more nuanced side of biology. There is not always one right answer, and issues of power and relationships often come into play.

phys-org.title: Molecular glasses solve long-standing Arrhenius paradox
phys-org.description: Glasses are non-crystalline but solid states of matter in which molecules and atoms are not arranged into a regular crystal lattice, but rather in a disordered pattern. Glassy materials are widely used in various settings, for instance, in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and the development of electronics or optical devices.

phys-org.title: Survey shows little shift in Americans' views on political violence
phys-org.description: A large, nationally representative survey of U.S. adults finds that support for, and willingness to engage in, political violence remained largely stable from mid-2024 to mid-2025, despite a highly contentious national election and ongoing political polarization, according to a study published in Injury Epidemiology.

phys-org.title: Icy moons' ability to host life could be revealed through an ecology-based method
phys-org.description: New observatories and spacecraft missions are probing environments in our solar system that could potentially host life but have long remained hidden. Icy moons like Saturn's Enceladus and Jupiter's Europa likely contain oceans beneath frozen outer shells. But a layer of ice prohibits space probes from sampling them directly.

phys-org.title: Strange winds on seven hot Jupiters reveal strongest signs yet of exoplanet magnetic activity
phys-org.description: A team of astronomers has found the strongest evidence yet that some planets outside our solar system may be magnetic. Using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT) and the Gemini North telescope, the researchers measured wind speeds on seven very hot, Jupiter-like exoplanets.

phys-org.title: Meteor as heavy as an elephant causes widespread speculation across New England
phys-org.description: When the double boom rang out in New England over the weekend, shaking homes and sending pets fleeing, questions started flooding social media.

phys-org.title: Biodiversity offsetting shows promise in pollinator conservation
phys-org.description: Newly created grassland habitats that compensate for nature lost to development can effectively support wild pollinators like bees and hoverflies, according to a first of its kind study in the Netherlands. The findings are published in the Journal of Applied Ecology.

phys-org.title: Making climate-neutral plastics and cosmetics using bacteria
phys-org.description: Plastics, medicines, cosmetics—there are very few everyday products that do not rely on using fossil resources. A European research team led by Charité—Universitätsmedizin Berlin is now aiming to revolutionize this cornerstone of the chemical industry: as part of the CarboNcare project, scientists are developing bacteria that can produce important chemical base materials from sustainable methanol—thereby replacing fossil resources.

phys-org.title: How the EU's carbon price on imports strengthens climate policies globally
phys-org.description: In early 2026, the EU extended its domestic carbon pricing to key products from beyond its borders. This is managed through the "Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism" (CBAM). Exporters of polluting goods to the EU must pay a climate tariff, unless their country has its own pricing scheme.

phys-org.title: Why the world's most ambitious coal phase‑out deal has failed, and what it means for climate finance
phys-org.description: In December 2025, Indonesia quietly abandoned plans to close the Cirebon-1 coal power plant.

phys-org.title: Roman telescope's massive infrared mirror is ready to fly
phys-org.description: NASA has completed its final inspection of the primary mirror on the Roman Space Telescope, which measures 2.4 meters (7.9 feet) in diameter and contains a layer of silver hundreds of times thinner than a human hair, at 400 nanometers.

phys-org.title: ESA selects two new scout-class missions
phys-org.description: When it comes to understanding Earth and our changing environment, space is the place. Not only does it give us an overall holistic view of the planet below, but satellite-based imagery can transcend national boundaries and give us an understanding of key changes that often go unseen at ground level.

phys-org.title: Rovers, regolith, robots: The blueprint for the moon
phys-org.description: The "soil" blanketing the moon's surface isn't actually soil. It's a fine, lethal, abrasive powder of shattered rock and jagged glass that shreds gaskets, chews through seals, and hangs in an airless environment blasted by unfiltered radiation and temperature swings that can warp steel. Scientists call it lunar regolith.

phys-org.title: Textile wastewater treatment generates alarmingly high levels of toxic compounds, study reveals
phys-org.description: Textile wastewater treatment practices inadvertently produce toxic byproducts—including chloroform and bromoform—at alarming levels that pose a clear occupational health hazard and lead to unknown environmental effects downstream, University of Massachusetts Amherst researchers have found. The study is published in the Journal of Hazardous Materials.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering
proj-syn.description: The productivity growth that transformed agriculture across Latin America and the Caribbean has slowed sharply in recent years, with farmers increasingly relying on costly inputs rather than efficiency gains. Without sustained public investment, the region risks losing competitiveness and reversing decades of hard-won progress.

proj-syn.title: Americans Can’t Afford Trump’s Economy
proj-syn.description: Prices are rising faster than wages in the US, and President Donald Trump’s policies are a key reason why. Now is the time for the Democratic Party to advance a credible and specific “affordability platform” that addresses the biggest culprits, from tariffs and energy prices to mass deportation of immigrants.

proj-syn.title: Britain’s Center Cannot Hold
proj-syn.description: A combination of globalization, deindustrialization, and other forces destroyed the old model of party politics that long prevailed in developed democracies. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the United Kingdom, where voters are angry and demanding radical solutions that no political leader can actually deliver.

proj-syn.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. But expanding the number of non-negotiable positions reduces the space for effective diplomacy and raises the risk of accidental conflict.
